body: Legend of Legaia is Prokion's PlayStation role-playing game, released in Japan on 29 October 1998 with production by Contrail. Humanity once depended on magical creatures called Seru, but a spreading Mist has turned them violent and broken much of civilisation. Vahn leaves the village of Rim Elm with Meta, a Ra-Seru unaffected by the Mist, seeking to restore the Genesis Trees that can drive it away. Noa and Gala join the journey. The story gives the party a visible reason to enter dangerous territory: each restored tree can make an inhabited place safe again.

The Tactical Arts System asks the player to build an attack from a sequence of directional commands. Confirming the choice makes the character perform those blows, while particular orders produce stronger Arts. Compatible sequences can overlap, allowing techniques to join into a longer combination. The Spirit command reduces incoming damage and prepares a longer attack on the next turn. That makes waiting an active choice: defend now to create a better opening later. Ordinary encounters become opportunities to learn the body's combinations as well as compare equipment, health and the enemy's remaining strength.

Ra-Seru change the party's attacks and let characters absorb the essence of certain defeated Seru. Those creatures can then be summoned at a magic-point cost, adding another use for encounters already completed. Arts use a separate resource, recovered through attacks, damage or Spirit, so physical combinations and magical assistance ask for different preparation. Michiru Ōshima composed the score for the journey. North American and European releases followed in 1999 and 2000. Legaia 2: Duel Saga later brought a separate cast to PlayStation 2, while the original remained centred on Vahn's struggle against the Mist.
